method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (the text's own no as FALSE, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); the rules in one module, the periods and the one regulative rule (s 52(1)) in a small module that alone imports daydate, the questions in a seat module importing both; the regulative rule run by EVALTRACE inside an exported question that takes only plain facts and dates; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Public Interest Disclosure Act 2013 (Cth), No. 133, 2013, Compilation No. 20 (compilation date 4 June 2026, register id C2026C00225), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2013A00133.txt (text sha256 b93102fea525a64a878a438ce44037eb22bbf5179c2f8bc3d7473b868d0accb7 per its .meta.json), retrieved 2026-10-13. No uncommenced amendments in the endnotes.

seat: the discloser: a current or former Commonwealth public official (or a person an authorised officer has determined under s 70 is treated as one) who has made or is thinking of making a disclosure of wrongdoing and may meet a reprisal for it; and, for ss 12A and 12B, the same person as a witness who helped with someone else's disclosure (pid-seat.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run pid-rules.l4 ; l4 run pid-dates.l4 ; l4 run pid-seat.l4 ; l4 run pid-cases.l4
checks.result: 170 assertions written, 170 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: The provisions a discloser meets when bringing or answering a claim. In: ss 10, 11, 11A, 12, 12A, 12B, 13, 14, 15(1), 16, 17, 18; the penalties of ss 19(1), (2), 20(1), (2), 67(1); s 20(1)-(4); s 22A; s 26(1) items 1-4, (1A), (2A); s 28; s 29 with ss 29A, 30(1); ss 31, 32(1), 33, 34; s 43(11); s 52(1)-(3), (6); s 69(1), (4); s 70(1), (3A). Out: ss 1-8 as a whole, 15(2), 19 beyond its penalties, 19A (stated), 21, 22, 23, 24, 26(2), 27, the definitions glossed in inputs (ss 30(2)-(4), 32(2)-(4), 35, 36, 41), the rest of Part 3, Part 4 and Part 5 (officials' machinery, or no fixed period). Reasons in NOTES.md.
